image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) standing on a sandy or dirt ground. The duck features the characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, grey/brown body plumage, and yellow bill. It is captured in a walking pose with one orange webbed foot visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellowish-green, matching the description perfectly.
The eye is visible as a small dark spot on the green head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is consistent with a duck, appearing compact and covered in smooth, dense-looking feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and greyish-brown body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One leg is clearly visible, showing the correct orange color, position, and webbed foot structure.
The folded wing is visible on the side, showing proper feather layering and shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear, showing the characteristic upward curl of the central feathers typical of mallard drakes.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Mallard Drake) and rule out hybrid or misclassified bird types.
To verify the anatomical correctness of the legs, feet, and wing folding, ensuring no extra limbs or structural melting.
To check for edge bleeding between the feathers and the background, and ensure the plumage texture is continuous without patchiness.
To assess overall sharpness, lighting consistency, and detect any subtle noise or texture anomalies in the ground or feathers.

focus_areas: Feather texture continuity and edge sharpness
Anatomical correctness of the webbed foot and leg joint
Color gradient on the iridescent green head
Shadow consistency under the body and feet
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the green head and the white neck ring; AI often blurs this boundary. Verify that the webbed foot does not show fused toes or unnatural geometry. Check if the shadow cast by the duck matches the lighting direction and intensity.
